observations: A wide open mouth fills the lower half, outlined in thick black with two rows of yellow and blue rectangular blocks set against a mint-green ground.

Two eye areas use concentric spiral lines in contrasting palettes: the left eye is ringed in solid purple with white swirl marks; the right eye layers orange, yellow, and red spirals around a blue dot.
Long red lines run diagonally across the entire image in loose strokes, crossing over black outlines, yellow fills, and the green ground without following the underlying forms.
reading: The face is all exposure — mouth forced wide, eyes wound into tight spirals that read as strain rather than sight. Red lines cut across everything, refusing to stay inside any boundary. The left eye's purple ring and the right eye's warm spiral create an asymmetry that feels less like a flaw than a split state. The mint-green ground keeps the whole from tipping into pure aggression.
contextAngle: Within the owned scrimshaw subset, this work shares its title number with a same-title variant (the comparison work), which uses a yellow ground, looser line weight, and a more open face structure — a direct formal contrast at the same title position. Title order and recorded creation order place these two works differently.

connections.reason: The same-title variant uses a yellow ground with loose blue and brown lines and a more open face structure, making the mint-green ground and dense red overlines of the primary work feel heightened by direct comparison.
nnxyz #31 shares paired spiral eye forms, a wide zigzag tooth row, and a yellow-green ground as structural anchors — the formal overlap the collector relates across the two collections.

lookingQuestion: The red lines cross the black outlines without following them — where exactly do they start and stop relative to the face's edges, and does that change how contained or uncontained the face feels?
ambiguities: Two works share the title Scrimshaw6 in the owned subset; title order and recorded creation order place them differently, so neither can be confirmed as a revision or earlier state of the other.
Scrimshaw5 shares a yellow ground and spiral eyes with the primary work but was not selected as a connection because the formal contrast with the same-title variant is more specific and direct.
